analysis:
MARKET REGIME: SPY in uptrend (+0.4% vs SMA50, 20d slope +1.13%) — constructive backdrop but not a reason to force new positions.

PORTFOLIO REVIEW:
• A (Agilent, +6.68%): Thesis intact. Uptrend extending, earnings in 23 days (Aug 26) — existing holders should be aware of binary event risk. No action needed but watch for pre-earnings volatility; consider whether to trim ahead of the print if position feels large.
• AMP (+4.85%): Small position, trending well, hold.
• CI (-5.30%): Weakest position. Managed care sector continues to face political/regulatory headwinds and elevated medical cost ratio concerns industry-wide. At $280.50 vs entry $296.21, stop has not been triggered (estimated ATR-based stop near $265-270), but this is the one to watch most carefully. Thesis is strained — any further deterioration or sector headline should prompt reassessment. No forced sell today, but CI is on a short leash.
• LMT (+4.11%): Defense spending tailwinds intact, hold.
• MCO (+1.53%): Quality compounder early in move, hold.

CAPACITY ANALYSIS: We are at 5 positions (67% deployed), which is the upper bound of the 3-5 position target. Headroom for new buys is $28,104. Adding a 6th position would exceed the concentration discipline. To initiate a new position, a current holding would need to be closed — and with only CI offering a legitimate case for early exit (thesis under pressure but stop not hit), forcing that trade to redeploy into a new name is not sufficiently asymmetric to justify today.

CANDIDATE NOTES: FDS screens attractively (37% of range, basing, fwd P/E 13.36, ROE 27%, two prior winning trades) and would be the first call if capacity opens. APH, NTRS, DAL, TRV all extended (>80% of range or far above SMA200) — avoid per rules. IR and COF are interesting on valuation but not enough urgency to displace existing positions.

CONCLUSION: Portfolio is full. No thesis breaks have triggered forced exits. The disciplined move is to hold the book, monitor CI closely, and keep cash dry. Forcing a 6th position or churning CI into FDS without a stop trigger would be manufacturing activity, not alpha. Cash is a position.
